item.content:encoded:
Lorena Puica had a successful corporate career, but health issues prompted a re-evaluation that led her to launch the AI-enabled wellness monitoring startup Syd Life AI in 2016.

Headquartered in the United Kingdom, with subsidiaries in Japan and the UAE, Syd Life AI measures quality of life and helps both individuals and institutions improve it. The company has been commercially operating since 2022 and is backed by more than a decade of research and development.

“There is no shortage of health data. The hard part is turning it into something a person, or a population, can act on,” Puica told Disrupt Africa.

Puica began her career in strategy consulting and investment banking, where she looked after more than US$200 billion. She holds five degrees across mathematics, finance and economics, and is a CFA charterholder.

item.content:encoded:
Ethiopian gaming startup Rise of Fearless has raised US$1 million in funding from advisory firm Epic Edges Capital as it looks to scale its African history-inspired battle royale mobile game.

Launched in 2025, Rise of Fearless offers an African take on the battle royale genre, drawing narrative inspiration from Ethiopia’s victory over Italian forces at the Battle of Adwa in 1896. The game’s characters, environments, hairstyles and attire are designed to reflect African identities, offering an alternative to the Western-centric narratives that have long dominated mainstream gaming.

Free-to-play on the Apple App Store and Google Play, the game has surpassed 15,000 downloads to date, with its largest player communities in Nigeria, Ethiopia and South Africa.

The post SA-founded Water Ledger Global secures investment from Launch Africa appeared first on Disrupt Africa.
item.content:encoded:
South African-founded water data startup Water Ledger Global (WLG) has secured a strategic investment from Launch Africa to scale its shared trust infrastructure for water globally.

Founded in October 2024 by a South African team, with roots in Australia going back to 2016, WLG is the company behind Water Ledger, a platform that creates a single, trusted record of how much water there is, who is using it, and what it is worth. 

By breaking down data silos, it gives regulators, utilities, investors and lenders a shared source of truth, with the aim of turning water into a transparent, investable asset class. The startup has subsidiaries in South Africa, Australia and the United States, and its technology is already live. Its SWaN solution for mitigation and nutrient markets operates in Virginia, while its water accounting and trading solution is used by Seqwater in Australia.

item.content:encoded:
Nigerian e-health startup Helium Health has received a US$2.5 million grant from Google.org to roll out artificial intelligence (AI) solutions that improve maternal healthcare delivery in the country.

Founded in 2016, Helium Health takes hospitals and clinics instantly digital with its flagship Electronic Medical Records/Hospital Management Information System (EMR/HMIS) product, the most widely used such solution in West Africa.  

The company is among 15 global recipients of the US$30 million Google.org Impact Challenge: AI for Government Innovation. The initiative backs organisations that work with governments to improve public service delivery.

item.content:encoded:
The United Kingdom (UK) has emerged as a key international base for African tech companies, offering a mix of incorporation, operations and regulatory licensing that sets it apart from other global markets, according to a new report.

TLP Advisory, a cross-border venture law practice with its origins in Nigeria, has released its third annual report, Home and Away: Tracking African Tech’s Global Footprint, which examined 100 tech companies across Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, Egypt, Ghana and Morocco, and their affiliations with the UK, US and UAE.

The post Nigeria’s Grey secures CBN approval to operate as IMTO appeared first on Disrupt Africa.
item.content:encoded:
Nigerian startup Grey, the Y Combinator-backed cross-border payment platform, has received approval from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to operate as an International Money Transfer Operator (IMTO) in the country.

Grey enables individuals and businesses to easily own and manage multi-currency accounts in USD, GBP, and EUR, supporting transfers to more than 170 destinations. It also offers access to virtual cards. 

Disrupt Africa reported in September the startup was now enabling direct payout to Senegal, Ivory Coast, Cameroon and Rwanda, and the CBN approval now allows Grey to facilitate inbound international money transfers into Nigeria, covering person-to-person, business-to-person and business-to-business payments.

The post Nigeria’s Mytherapist wants to close the gap between needing therapy and getting it appeared first on Disrupt Africa.
item.content:encoded:
Nigerian startup Mytherapist is helping people find qualified therapists, book appointments and attend sessions via video, audio or chat, while also offering tools to support their wellbeing between sessions.

Founded in 2021 by Oluwaseun Raphael Afolayan and Dedoyin Ajayi, Mytherapist launched a pilot in October 2022 before going public and beginning paid therapy bookings in January 2023. 

“The idea came from the difficulty of finding reliable, affordable support during the pandemic and the aftermath of the EndSARS protests. That experience affected me and people around me,” Afolayan told Disrupt Africa.

Mytherapist is built around what Afolayan describes as the practical questions people face when looking for help. “Who should I speak to? What will it cost? When are they available? How do I fit a session into my day?” he said.

item.content:encoded:
Moroccan ed-tech startup PhiDoc has launched an integrated research platform designed to give African PhD candidates and early-career researchers coordinated access to funding information, mentorship and peer networks.

Founded earlier this year by Oussama Elasri and two co-founders, PhiDoc went live in September, mapping thesis progress, surfacing funding calls and conference opportunities filtered by discipline and career stage, and offering a researcher directory for networking and collaboration. 

It also includes a research assistant for methodology support and connects emerging researchers with mentors across the continent.

The post How Kenya’s PayServe is building the operating layer for managed real estate appeared first on Disrupt Africa.
item.content:encoded:
Kenyan prop-tech and fintech startup PayServe is raising a US$1 million Series A round as it scales a platform that automates billing, payments and reconciliation for the country’s fast-growing managed estates.

Founded in 2024, PayServe provides revenue assurance for managed real estate, handling billing for rent, service charge and utilities across gated communities, large apartment estates and mixed-use developments.

“Our platform reads consumption straight from our smart water and power meters, collects payments through M-Pesa and direct bank integrations with Absa, Co-op Bank, NCBA, Equity and KCB, and reconciles them automatically,” founder and CEO Steve Butler told Disrupt Africa. “It then posts everything to the client’s accounting system, such as SAP, Zoho or QuickBooks, with KRA eTIMS compliance built in.”
